## 2026-11-25 12:33 PST — Doubling-norm exactness criterion

### What was done

Proved that scalar 2 generates the quotient by the first
remaining P-192 subgroup, using its checked order in the
scalar quotient. Since 2 is a scalar square and the y product
already transforms correctly inside the subgroup, full sign
exactness is equivalent to invariance under doubling at every
nonzero marking. Derived the doubling sextic and an x-only
resultant norm for that ratio. Added a pure-Python finite replay
on two order-97 curves over F_79: the positive curve has zero
doubling/exactness mismatches; the negative curve has 32 of
each. The replay checks the sextic ratio and product norm
at all 48 signed classes on both curves. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Use the doubling norm as a precise symbolic exactness or
falsification target. A dense subgroup polynomial at the
P-192 size is far beyond the memory gate, so the identity
alone does not supply an efficient evaluator. [pcc:unverified]

### Open threads

Find a compressed evaluation or a P-192 witness for the
doubling norm, then measure a correct cold sign evaluator
against the rho reference. [pcc:unverified]

### Errors

Sage could not create a cache file because the system data
volume is full. The independent pure-Python control avoided
that cache and ran to completion. Conductor recovered after
its earlier internal errors, and the stale claim was released.
[pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-25 12:56 PST — Fundamental CM discriminant gate

### What was done

Checked P-192's trace and Frobenius discriminant from its
published field and group orders. PARI/GP factored the
discriminant into four distinct primes and certified each
with `isprime`; the reproducible check is
`cm_endomorphism_gate.gp`. The discriminant is fundamental,
so the standard ordinary-curve order inclusions give
`End_Fp(E)=Z[pi]`. The norm form proves every noninteger
endomorphism has degree at least `ceil(|D|/4)`, about
`2^191.941`. PARI/GP also checks that 2 and 3 are inert
and 13 splits, giving a 52-edge lower bound for a cycle
repeatedly following one degree-13 ideal direction.
Using the repository's optimized odd-isogeny formula, such
a 52-edge chain would cost at least 4625M+51S to move one
point, before kernel and map construction. The currently
selected direct scalar step is 1045M+1165S including its
projective product update; these are formula counts only.
[pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Treat this as a limit on low-degree CM self-map shortcuts,
not on arbitrary horizontal isogeny chains or their
evaluation time. Keep the doubling-norm exactness gate open.
[pcc:unverified]

### Open threads

Find an exact P-192 sign evaluation or a witness against the
large coset. A level-structure chain proposal must specify
its ideal sequence and charge construction and point action;
the discriminant gate alone does not price that action.
[pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-25 13:14 PST — Degree-13 ideal-class cycle check

### What was done

Extended `cm_endomorphism_gate.gp` to construct the reduced
prime form above 13 and compose its class through one
million powers. No power returned to the principal class;
the final iterated form equals an independent `qfbpow` at
exponent one million. A discriminant -23 control detects
a return at the known third power, and an intentionally
mutated assertion exits with status 1. Thus the repeated one-direction
degree-13 cycle has more than one million edges. The
existing optimized isogeny formula charges at least
90000035M+1000000S to move one point on such a cycle,
before kernel or map construction. A separate GP replay
screened `13^i 23^j 5^e5 11^e11 31^e31` class relations
for `|i|,|j|≤1000` and the three ramified exponents in
`{0,1}`. It found only the identity tuple. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made (and why)

## 2026-11-25 14:08 PST — Duplication-sextic factorization gate

### What was done

Derived from Frobenius on E[4] that `D2=psi4/(4y)` is irreducible over Fp whenever `p=3 mod 4` and `#E(Fp)=1 mod 4`. Cayley–Hamilton gives `F^3=2F-I` and `F^6=I` mod 4; the mod-2 characteristic polynomial `X^2+X+1` excludes shorter x-orbits. Exhaustively checked all eight compatible 2-by-2 matrices modulo 4 and 576 primitive-vector powers. The new `doubling_sextic_factor_gate.gp` confirms sextic irreducibility on P-192 and five small controls, including both exact and inexact coset signs. Added the proof and its limit to the report in PR #5199. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Factoring the fixed sextic cannot split the P-192 resultant into smaller base-field norms. Rewriting it as a character in F_(p^6) still requires evaluating the degree-m orbit polynomial; it is not a compressed evaluator. Research-KB revision `750797a540fb4c38837c67b12df84d5b` (refreshed 2026-11-25T03:19:48Z) returned no directly applicable compressed-evaluation source for three queries on elliptic periods, torsion norms, and ray actions; the existing report and its primary references guided this gate. already transforms correctly inside the subgroup, full sign

nonzero marking. Derived the doubling sextic and an x-only
resultant norm for that ratio. Added a pure-Python finite replay
on two order-97 curves over F_79: the positive curve has zero
doubling/exactness mismatches; the negative curve has 32 of
each. The replay checks the sextic ratio and product norm
at all 48 signed classes on both curves. [pcc:unverified]

falsification target. A dense subgroup polynomial at the

alone does not supply an efficient evaluator. [pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-25 12:56 PST — Fundamental CM discriminant gate

### What was done

Checked P-192's trace and Frobenius discriminant from its
published field and group orders. PARI/GP factored the
discriminant into four distinct primes and certified each
with `isprime`; the reproducible check is
`cm_endomorphism_gate.gp`. The discriminant is fundamental,
so the standard ordinary-curve order inclusions give
`End_Fp(E)=Z[pi]`. The norm form proves every noninteger
endomorphism has degree at least `ceil(|D|/4)`, about

and 13 splits, giving a 52-edge lower bound for a cycle
repeatedly following one degree-13 ideal direction.
Using the repository's optimized odd-isogeny formula, such
a 52-edge chain would cost at least 4625M+51S to move one
point, before kernel and map construction. The currently
selected direct scalar step is 1045M+1165S including its
projective product update; these are formula counts only.

Treat this as a limit on low-degree CM self-map shortcuts,
not on arbitrary horizontal isogeny chains or their
evaluation time. Keep the doubling-norm exactness gate open.

Find an exact P-192 sign evaluation or a witness against the
large coset. A level-structure chain proposal must specify

## 2026-11-25T19:15:15Z — Exact two-summand cycle-closure boundary (Codex, draft PR #5187)

### What was done (commands, files, features)

- Read the boundary ledger Sections 10.2 and 11.2-11.3, the November 18
  yield/rank frontier, and Zaslavsky 1982 Section 8A-8B. Primary PDF SHA-256
  `fa66ad267542e6b7cdbeef4706f7ca61d2f64fc8a478ed414d3428d4a3a12a4d`;
  Theorem 8B.1 and Corollary 8B.3 identify the signed-incidence dependency
  matroid away from characteristic two. Research KB and the named Lean instance
  skill were unavailable, so the repository literature-first/proof-gate path was
  used directly.
- Added `IcNegative/CycleClosure.lean`: an F3 triangle and self-pair loop with
  no nonzero unsigned row dependency, square and parallel-edge positive
  controls, and the exact nonzero target-projection recovery bridge. Installed the pinned Lean 4.34.1
  toolchain into a task cache; the module and full project build pass.
- Added `research/ic_cycle_closure_20261125/{README.md,verify.py}`. The independent
  stdlib enumeration passes and records the parameterized law
  `ops(F)=F^2/(4t)+2c#E rho(F/(2k))/F^2`.
- Added five graph nodes and four edges, refined
  `GAP-RP-CYCLE-CLOSURE-LAW`, made the `r^(1/6)` law explicitly conditional on
  `rho(K)=K/2`, and regenerated the graph/weakness/attack artifacts (659 nodes,
  1,077 edges, 246 sources). Reconciled the recovered Theriault primary SHA and
  downgraded its algorithm node to conditional: the recorded finite Theorem 1
  counterexample is not presented as an exponent refutation. [pcc:unverified]
- GitHub's full corpus, artifact-freshness, validation, PCC, learning, size,
  parity, and native Rust checks passed for implementation commit
  `e8df2d7ee60db4f90cddd51b87816eca602268d3`.

### Decisions made (and why)

- Replace “first cycle” by “first useful balanced circuit with nonzero target
  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block
  has rank `v-1` when bipartite and `v` when non-bipartite; a lone odd cycle is
  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.
- Keep the stopping law open. The exact graph algebra does not establish the
  edge/sign ensemble, concentration, arrival exponent, or target-projection
  distribution needed by the family extrapolation.

- Capture a complete, non-stopped natural two-summand relation stream and
  estimate the first balanced-circuit and first useful-projection stopping laws
  separately, excluding repeated targets.
- Build the smallest exact solver-visibility cell from the same immutable
  population; continue the reusable/right-rank branch independently.
- Repair Theriault's printed finite collision lemma and check whether the repair
  suffices for every step of the stated asymptotic balance.

### Decisions made

- Sources checked: the original derivation in §2.2; `workspace:docs/notes/p-vs-np-20261124/04-eps0-calculation.md`, which reached the same correction independently, as did fleet notes B2 and R. KB unavailable: no research-kb server in this cloud container.

remaining P-192 subgroup, using its checked order in the
scalar quotient. Since 2 is a scalar square and the y product
already transforms correctly inside the subgroup, full sign
exactness is equivalent to invariance under doubling at every
nonzero marking. Derived the doubling sextic and an x-only
resultant norm for that ratio. Added a pure-Python finite replay
on two order-97 curves over F_79: the positive curve has zero
doubling/exactness mismatches; the negative curve has 32 of
each. The replay checks the sextic ratio and product norm
at all 48 signed classes on both curves. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Use the doubling norm as a precise symbolic exactness or
falsification target. A dense subgroup polynomial at the
P-192 size is far beyond the memory gate, so the identity
alone does not supply an efficient evaluator. [pcc:unverified]

### Open threads

Find a compressed evaluation or a P-192 witness for the
doubling norm, then measure a correct cold sign evaluator
against the rho reference. [pcc:unverified]

### Errors

Sage could not create a cache file because the system data
volume is full. The independent pure-Python control avoided
that cache and ran to completion. Conductor recovered after
its earlier internal errors, and the stale claim was released.

## 2026-11-25 12:33 PST — Doubling-norm exactness criterion

### What was done

Proved that scalar 2 generates the quotient by the first
remaining P-192 subgroup, using its checked order in the
scalar quotient. Since 2 is a scalar square and the y product
already transforms correctly inside the subgroup, full sign
exactness is equivalent to invariance under doubling at every
nonzero marking. Derived the doubling sextic and an x-only
resultant norm for that ratio. Added a pure-Python finite replay
on two order-97 curves over F_79: the positive curve has zero

## 2026-11-25T20:05:00Z — Retention study redesigned (v2): online admission under a memory cap (PR #5186)

### What was done (commands, files, features)
- The user asked whether the v1 design made sense; on review it did not. Its metric, LP left
  nullity, saturates far above the factor-base size (14,738 against a needed rank of 14). Its
  offline policies needed the whole batch, which contradicts a memory budget. Auto-merge was
  disabled and the PR returned to draft.
- Rewrote `large_prime_graph::retention`:
  - `AdmissionRule` (all, complete_only, first_come, singles_only, max_lp, seen_lp);
  - `simulate_admission`, which harvests cycles on arrival through `ForestWitnessExtractor`;
  - `IncrementalRank`;
  - the score is the draw at which the useful factor-base rank reaches its target.
- Moved the F_p* toy collector to `examples/lp_retention_support/fp_toy.rs`.
- Tests (5): rank equals `audit_projected_rank`; every harvested relation replays through
  `replay_complete_relation`; `all` ≥ rule ≥ `complete_only` at every draw; caps and rule
  semantics; F_p* replay. Wrapper results: 41/41 + 5/5. clippy -D warnings clean on all PR targets.
- Protocol v2 frozen at 2bffd4df4 before data. Results (`research/lp_retention_20261125/RESULTS_V2.md`):
  - F_p*: partials cut draws to full rank 1.65–2.09×; under a binding cap, a tighter LP bound is the
    rule that beats first_come.
  - Real binary n = 20/24 streams: partials are worth 18.6–97×, and singles_only is 3–6× from `all`
    at 10×|FB| on n = 20, where first_come and seen_lp stay near complete-only.
  - This reverses v1's "retention barely matters on the real stream".

### Decisions made (and why)
- Admission-only (no eviction) model: deployable in a streaming collector and analysable (the
  ordering guarantee is a theorem). Eviction is left open.
- Kept the v1 results as a marked superseded section rather than deleting them; their exact counts
  are correct, only the design was wrong.

- Price draws (point-decomposition cost) and model eviction.
- More real streams (Koblitz orbit, Joux–Vitse two-LP).

- The v1 design flaw itself (above).
- A calibration coincidence (identical draws for B = 512 and 1024 on one seed), traced: the stream

## 2026-11-25T20:05:00Z — Retention study redesigned (v2): online admission under a memory cap (PR #5186)

### What was done (commands, files, features)
- The user asked whether the v1 design made sense; on review it did not. Its metric, LP left
  nullity, saturates far above the factor-base size (14,738 against a needed rank of 14). Its
  offline policies needed the whole batch, which contradicts a memory budget. Auto-merge was
  disabled and the PR returned to draft.
- Rewrote `large_prime_graph::retention`:
  - `AdmissionRule` (all, complete_only, first_come, singles_only, max_lp, seen_lp);
  - `simulate_admission`, which harvests cycles on arrival through `ForestWitnessExtractor`;
  - `IncrementalRank`;
  - the score is the draw at which the useful factor-base rank reaches its target.
- Moved the F_p* toy collector to `examples/lp_retention_support/fp_toy.rs`.
- Tests (5): rank equals `audit_projected_rank`; every harvested relation replays through
  `replay_complete_relation`; `all` ≥ rule ≥ `complete_only` at every draw; caps and rule
  semantics; F_p* replay. Wrapper results: 41/41 + 5/5. clippy -D warnings clean on all PR targets.
- Protocol v2 frozen at 2bffd4df4 before data. Results (`research/lp_retention_20261125/RESULTS_V2.md`):
  - F_p*: partials cut draws to full rank 1.65–2.09×; under a binding cap, a tighter LP bound is the
    rule that beats first_come.
  - Real binary n = 20/24 streams: partials are worth 18.6–97×, and singles_only is 3–6× from `all`
    at 10×|FB| on n = 20, where first_come and seen_lp stay near complete-only.
  - This reverses v1's "retention barely matters on the real stream".

### Decisions made (and why)
- Admission-only (no eviction) model: deployable in a streaming collector and analysable (the
  ordering guarantee is a theorem). Eviction is left open.
- Kept the v1 results as a marked superseded section rather than deleting them; their exact counts
  are correct, only the design was wrong.

### Open threads (unfinished, pick up next time)
- Price draws (point-decomposition cost) and model eviction.
- More real streams (Koblitz orbit, Joux–Vitse two-LP).

### Errors (what went wrong, how it was handled)
- The v1 design flaw itself (above).
- A calibration coincidence (identical draws for B = 512 and 1024 on one seed), traced: the stream
  recomputes exactly in Python, and three other seeds differ.
## 2026-11-25T19:15:15Z — Exact two-summand cycle-closure boundary (Codex, draft PR #5187)

### What was done (commands, files, features)

- Read the boundary ledger Sections 10.2 and 11.2-11.3, the November 18
  yield/rank frontier, and Zaslavsky 1982 Section 8A-8B. Primary PDF SHA-256
  `fa66ad267542e6b7cdbeef4706f7ca61d2f64fc8a478ed414d3428d4a3a12a4d`;
  Theorem 8B.1 and Corollary 8B.3 identify the signed-incidence dependency
  matroid away from characteristic two. Research KB and the named Lean instance
  skill were unavailable, so the repository literature-first/proof-gate path was
  used directly.
- Added `IcNegative/CycleClosure.lean`: an F3 triangle and self-pair loop with
  no nonzero unsigned row dependency, square and parallel-edge positive
  controls, and the exact nonzero target-projection recovery bridge. Installed the pinned Lean 4.34.1
  toolchain into a task cache; the module and full project build pass.
- Added `research/ic_cycle_closure_20261125/{README.md,verify.py}`. The independent
  stdlib enumeration passes and records the parameterized law
  `ops(F)=F^2/(4t)+2c#E rho(F/(2k))/F^2`.
- Added five graph nodes and four edges, refined
  `GAP-RP-CYCLE-CLOSURE-LAW`, made the `r^(1/6)` law explicitly conditional on
  `rho(K)=K/2`, and regenerated the graph/weakness/attack artifacts (659 nodes,
  1,077 edges, 246 sources). Reconciled the recovered Theriault primary SHA and
  downgraded its algorithm node to conditional: the recorded finite Theorem 1
  counterexample is not presented as an exponent refutation. [pcc:unverified]
- GitHub's full corpus, artifact-freshness, validation, PCC, learning, size,
  parity, and native Rust checks passed for implementation commit
  `e8df2d7ee60db4f90cddd51b87816eca602268d3`.

### Decisions made (and why)

- Replace “first cycle” by “first useful balanced circuit with nonzero target
  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block
  has rank `v-1` when bipartite and `v` when non-bipartite; a lone odd cycle is
  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.
- Keep the stopping law open. The exact graph algebra does not establish the
  edge/sign ensemble, concentration, arrival exponent, or target-projection
  distribution needed by the family extrapolation.

### Open threads (unfinished, pick up next time)

- Capture a complete, non-stopped natural two-summand relation stream and
  estimate the first balanced-circuit and first useful-projection stopping laws
  separately, excluding repeated targets.
- Build the smallest exact solver-visibility cell from the same immutable
  population; continue the reusable/right-rank branch independently.
- Repair Theriault's printed finite collision lemma and check whether the repair
  suffices for every step of the stated asymptotic balance.

  simplified-SWU (RFC 9380 §6.6.2) orbit factor base and Semaev `S_4` in the elementary

  claimed the S_3⊗S_3 resultant while computing the parabola resultant; singular-curve check
  added; HashMap → HashSet.

### Decisions made (and why)

  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block

  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.
- Keep the stopping law open. The exact graph algebra does not establish the
  edge/sign ensemble, concentration, arrival exponent, or target-projection
  distribution needed by the family extrapolation.

## 2026-11-25 12:56 PST — Fundamental CM discriminant gate

### What was done

Checked P-192's trace and Frobenius discriminant from its
published field and group orders. PARI/GP factored the
discriminant into four distinct primes and certified each
with `isprime`; the reproducible check is
`cm_endomorphism_gate.gp`. The discriminant is fundamental,
so the standard ordinary-curve order inclusions give
`End_Fp(E)=Z[pi]`. The norm form proves every noninteger
endomorphism has degree at least `ceil(|D|/4)`, about
`2^191.941`. PARI/GP also checks that 2 and 3 are inert
and 13 splits, giving a 52-edge lower bound for a cycle
repeatedly following one degree-13 ideal direction.
Using the repository's optimized odd-isogeny formula, such
a 52-edge chain would cost at least 4625M+51S to move one
point, before kernel and map construction. The currently
selected direct scalar step is 1045M+1165S including its
projective product update; these are formula counts only.
[pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Treat this as a limit on low-degree CM self-map shortcuts,
not on arbitrary horizontal isogeny chains or their
evaluation time. Keep the doubling-norm exactness gate open.
[pcc:unverified]

### Open threads

Find an exact P-192 sign evaluation or a witness against the
large coset. A level-structure chain proposal must specify
its ideal sequence and charge construction and point action;
the discriminant gate alone does not price that action.
[pcc:unverified]

### Errors

The first report insertion missed its line context and was
reapplied at the exact paragraph boundary. The GP replay
passed. [pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-25 13:14 PST — Degree-13 ideal-class cycle check

### What was done

Extended `cm_endomorphism_gate.gp` to construct the reduced
prime form above 13 and compose its class through one
million powers. No power returned to the principal class;
the final iterated form equals an independent `qfbpow` at
exponent one million. A discriminant -23 control detects
a return at the known third power, and an intentionally
mutated assertion exits with status 1. Thus the repeated one-direction
degree-13 cycle has more than one million edges. The
existing optimized isogeny formula charges at least
90000035M+1000000S to move one point on such a cycle,
before kernel or map construction. A separate GP replay
screened `13^i 23^j 5^e5 11^e11 31^e31` class relations
for `|i|,|j|≤1000` and the three ramified exponents in
`{0,1}`. It found only the identity tuple. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Stop treating a short pure degree-13 return cycle or a
short relation in the checked 13/23/5/11/31 class box as a
candidate scalar-orbit step. Other mixed ideal paths and a
compressed direct doubling norm remain separate questions.
[pcc:unverified]

Check any concrete mixed horizontal path only with its
ideal relation, point-action cost, and a sign exactness

### Decisions made (and why)

  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block

  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.

  edge/sign ensemble, concentration, arrival exponent, or target-projection
  distribution needed by the family extrapolation.

Proved that scalar 2 generates the quotient by the first
remaining P-192 subgroup, using its checked order in the
scalar quotient. Since 2 is a scalar square and the y product
already transforms correctly inside the subgroup, full sign
exactness is equivalent to invariance under doubling at every
nonzero marking. Derived the doubling sextic and an x-only
resultant norm for that ratio. Added a pure-Python finite replay
on two order-97 curves over F_79: the positive curve has zero
doubling/exactness mismatches; the negative curve has 32 of
each. The replay checks the sextic ratio and product norm
at all 48 signed classes on both curves. [pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Use the doubling norm as a precise symbolic exactness or
falsification target. A dense subgroup polynomial at the
P-192 size is far beyond the memory gate, so the identity
alone does not supply an efficient evaluator. [pcc:unverified]

### Open threads

Find a compressed evaluation or a P-192 witness for the
doubling norm, then measure a correct cold sign evaluator
against the rho reference. [pcc:unverified]

### Errors

Sage could not create a cache file because the system data
volume is full. The independent pure-Python control avoided
that cache and ran to completion. Conductor recovered after
its earlier internal errors, and the stale claim was released.
[pcc:unverified]

## 2026-11-25 12:56 PST — Fundamental CM discriminant gate

### What was done

Checked P-192's trace and Frobenius discriminant from its
published field and group orders. PARI/GP factored the
discriminant into four distinct primes and certified each
with `isprime`; the reproducible check is
`cm_endomorphism_gate.gp`. The discriminant is fundamental,
so the standard ordinary-curve order inclusions give
`End_Fp(E)=Z[pi]`. The norm form proves every noninteger
endomorphism has degree at least `ceil(|D|/4)`, about
`2^191.941`. PARI/GP also checks that 2 and 3 are inert
and 13 splits, giving a 52-edge lower bound for a cycle
repeatedly following one degree-13 ideal direction.
Using the repository's optimized odd-isogeny formula, such
a 52-edge chain would cost at least 4625M+51S to move one
point, before kernel and map construction. The currently
selected direct scalar step is 1045M+1165S including its
projective product update; these are formula counts only.
[pcc:unverified]

### Decisions made

Treat this as a limit on low-degree CM self-map shortcuts,
not on arbitrary horizontal isogeny chains or their
evaluation time. Keep the doubling-norm exactness gate open.
[pcc:unverified]

Find an exact P-192 sign evaluation or a witness against the
large coset. A level-structure chain proposal must specify
its ideal sequence and charge construction and point action;
the discriminant gate alone does not price that action.

## 2026-11-25T20:05:00Z — Retention study redesigned (v2): online admission under a memory cap (PR #5186)

### What was done (commands, files, features)
- The user asked whether the v1 design made sense; on review it did not. Its metric, LP left
  nullity, saturates far above the factor-base size (14,738 against a needed rank of 14). Its
  offline policies needed the whole batch, which contradicts a memory budget. Auto-merge was
  disabled and the PR returned to draft.

  - `AdmissionRule` (all, complete_only, first_come, singles_only, max_lp, seen_lp);
  - `simulate_admission`, which harvests cycles on arrival through `ForestWitnessExtractor`;
  - `IncrementalRank`;
  - the score is the draw at which the useful factor-base rank reaches its target.
- Moved the F_p* toy collector to `examples/lp_retention_support/fp_toy.rs`.
- Tests (5): rank equals `audit_projected_rank`; every harvested relation replays through
  `replay_complete_relation`; `all` ≥ rule ≥ `complete_only` at every draw; caps and rule
  semantics; F_p* replay. Wrapper results: 41/41 + 5/5. clippy -D warnings clean on all PR targets.
- Protocol v2 frozen at 2bffd4df4 before data. Results (`research/lp_retention_20261125/RESULTS_V2.md`):
  - F_p*: partials cut draws to full rank 1.65–2.09×; under a binding cap, a tighter LP bound is the
    rule that beats first_come.
  - Real binary n = 20/24 streams: partials are worth 18.6–97×, and singles_only is 3–6× from `all`
    at 10×|FB| on n = 20, where first_come and seen_lp stay near complete-only.
  - This reverses v1's "retention barely matters on the real stream".

### Decisions made (and why)
- Admission-only (no eviction) model: deployable in a streaming collector and analysable (the
  ordering guarantee is a theorem). Eviction is left open.
- Kept the v1 results as a marked superseded section rather than deleting them; their exact counts
  are correct, only the design was wrong.

  skill were unavailable, so the repository literature-first/proof-gate path was
  used directly.
- Added `IcNegative/CycleClosure.lean`: an F3 triangle and self-pair loop with
  no nonzero unsigned row dependency, square and parallel-edge positive
  controls, and the exact nonzero target-projection recovery bridge. Installed the pinned Lean 4.34.1
  toolchain into a task cache; the module and full project build pass.
- Added `research/ic_cycle_closure_20261125/{README.md,verify.py}`. The independent
  stdlib enumeration passes and records the parameterized law
  `ops(F)=F^2/(4t)+2c#E rho(F/(2k))/F^2`.
- Added five graph nodes and four edges, refined
  `GAP-RP-CYCLE-CLOSURE-LAW`, made the `r^(1/6)` law explicitly conditional on
  `rho(K)=K/2`, and regenerated the graph/weakness/attack artifacts (659 nodes,
  1,077 edges, 246 sources). Reconciled the recovered Theriault primary SHA and
  downgraded its algorithm node to conditional: the recorded finite Theorem 1
  counterexample is not presented as an exponent refutation. [pcc:unverified]

  parity, and native Rust checks passed for implementation commit
  `e8df2d7ee60db4f90cddd51b87816eca602268d3`.

### Decisions made (and why)

- Replace “first cycle” by “first useful balanced circuit with nonzero target
  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block
  has rank `v-1` when bipartite and `v` when non-bipartite; a lone odd cycle is
  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.
- Keep the stopping law open. The exact graph algebra does not establish the
  edge/sign ensemble, concentration, arrival exponent, or target-projection
  distribution needed by the family extrapolation.

  estimate the first balanced-circuit and first useful-projection stopping laws

### Decisions made (and why)

  projection.” Over an odd scalar field, a connected unsigned incidence block
  has rank `v-1` when bipartite and `v` when non-bipartite; a lone odd cycle is
  full rank. This is a theorem-level correction, not merely a looser constant.

## prime_swu_sym kernel (Claude Code, branch feat/prime-swu-sym-20261125, PR #5192)

### What was done (commands, files, features)

- Added `src/cryptanalysis/prime_swu_sym.rs` (registered in `src/cryptanalysis/mod.rs`):
  simplified-SWU (RFC 9380 §6.6.2) orbit factor base and Semaev `S_4` in the elementary
  symmetric functions `(e1, e2, e3)` of three abscissae, via the resultant of the cubic and
  quartic obtained from a parabola `y = αx² + βx + γ` through four points. u64 values with
  u128 products for any `p < 2^32`. `SymmetricM3Table::decompose_target` scans `i ≤ j ≤ k`
  (≈ B³/6 evaluations per target) and recovers signs by point addition.

  21 add with 2a/4b/8b precomputed; a no-op `chunks(w)` "window" removed; doc comment
  claimed the S_3⊗S_3 resultant while computing the parabola resultant; singular-curve check
  added; HashMap → HashSet.

  constant ratio on 300 tuples per prime, planted relations incl. vertical pairs vanish);
  agreement with `semaev_higher::s4_in_last_proper` (p = 10007, 2^31−1); fixed op count;

- Independently minimised the §2.2 reduction (λ = Δn/K² + log n, plus the 2^{n/K} table build): fitted 0.676 at β = 1 and 0.806 at β = ½. With the overhead dropped the fit is 0.53, falling toward ½, which is what the original text assumed.
- Sources checked: the original derivation in §2.2; `workspace:docs/notes/p-vs-np-20261124/04-eps0-calculation.md`, which reached the same correction independently, as did fleet notes B2 and R. KB unavailable: no research-kb server in this cloud container.

### Decisions made (and why)

- §3's information bound is left unchanged. Its cost `2^{max(U,K²)/K}` is a lower bound on the best case, and adding the overhead can only raise it, so the ECDLP-256 / Ring-LWE-1024 conclusion stands.
- The original claim is kept visible, marked as corrected rather than silently replaced, so citations of the 2026-11-22 version can be traced.

## prime_swu_sym kernel (Claude Code, branch feat/prime-swu-sym-20261125, PR #5192)

### What was done (commands, files, features)

- Added `src/cryptanalysis/prime_swu_sym.rs` (registered in `src/cryptanalysis/mod.rs`):
  simplified-SWU (RFC 9380 §6.6.2) orbit factor base and Semaev `S_4` in the elementary
  symmetric functions `(e1, e2, e3)` of three abscissae, via the resultant of the cubic and
  quartic obtained from a parabola `y = αx² + βx + γ` through four points. u64 values with

## 2026-11-25 12:56 PST — Fundamental CM discriminant gate

Checked P-192's trace and Frobenius discriminant from its

point, before kernel and map construction. The currently
selected direct scalar step is 1045M+1165S including its
projective product update; these are formula counts only.
